key_insight: Extending high-rate many-hypercube concatenated quantum codes from qubits to prime-dimensional qudits improves fault-tolerance, with thresholds rising as local dimension increases and reaching 10.0% at q = 13.
engineering_relevance: Higher-dimensional qudits can substantially reduce logical error rates for fault-tolerant quantum computing, making them attractive for more efficient code architectures and decoder design.
method: Constructed level-2 and level-3 qudit MHC codes with parameters [[6^2,4^2,2^2]]_q and [[6^3,4^3,2^3]]_q.
Generalized the level-by-level minimum-distance (LLMD) decoder from qubit to qudit codes.
Evaluated code-capacity performance under an X-error model for prime dimensions up to q = 13.
evidence_signal: In simulations, the error threshold increased monotonically with q, nearly doubling from 5.1% for qubits to 10.0% at q = 13, with a pronounced waterfall regime at larger q.
watch_item: The reported gains are for a qudit X-error model and code-capacity setting, so practical performance may differ under more realistic noise, hardware constraints, and full fault-tolerance overheads.
paper_title: High-Rate Concatenated Quantum Error-Correcting Codes for Qudits
